Aroids such as monstera, philodendron and pothos grow on trees in the wild and want an airy, fast-draining mix rather than dense compost. A common recipe is one part potting soil, one part orchid bark, one part perlite, with a handful of charcoal and worm castings. The chunky pieces keep air around the roots and prevent rot. Repot in spring, one pot size up, into a pot with drainage holes. This mix pairs with the watering advice in [[Monstera care]].
